subject: Brightly - implementation kickoff & access / API key plan
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@brightlyhealth.com>, Dave Hernandez <dave.hernandez@brightlyhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: Brightly - implementation kickoff & access / API key plan

Connor / engineering team — looping you in to start the tenant setup for Brightly Health (deal RDW-8421). Brightly is aiming for a pilot run the week of 2026-12-06; we have a 60-minute kickoff penciled for 2026-11-30 (Sara included below).

Summary of asks for initial setup (what the customer expects from Redwood before kickoff):
- Create a Brightly project/namespace in the us-west region (tag: brightly-prod)
- Seed two API keys: a) admin key scoped to workspace admin (for initial provisioning), b) telemetry-readonly key for metrics/usage ingestion
- Create an RBAC role mapping doc and invite 3 Brightly users (Sara, Dave, and one infra engineer) as Project Admins for the pilot
- Confirm whether Brightly wants keys as long-lived service keys or we should provision short-lived service accounts with rotation hooks (they mentioned Okta + an HSM in the RFI)

Attached is the mutual action plan we shared in the sales cycle (Brightly_MutualActionPlan_v1.xlsx). Marcus — can you confirm the default RBAC roles and whether we need the "service-account" pattern for telemetry ingestion, or if a scoped API key is sufficient?

Connor — recommend owning the API key seed and admin invites. Happy to introduce the Brightly stakeholders on the kickoff; they prefer morning PST.

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@brightlyhealth.com>, Dave Hernandez <dave.hernandez@brightlyhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Brightly - implementation kickoff & access / API key plan

Thanks Monica — I can take point on the provisioning. Quick clarifications before I seed anything: 
1) Two separate API credentials makes sense. We'll provide an "admin:project" key and a "telemetry:ingest" key. The admin key will be usable via the Console and REST; telemetry key will be scoped to write-only ingest endpoints.
2) For SSO/KMS: if Brightly is bringing Okta for SSO and wants keys backed by customer-managed KMS, we'll need the KMS key ARN (or HSM interface) prior to seeding — otherwise we'll create Redwood-managed keys and note rotation policies in the invite.
3) Do we need to create a service-account JSON for their infra (recommended for automation) or will the infra team call using the telemetry API key? Service-account enables shorter rotation windows and easier auditing.

I'll prepare an invite template (init-invite-template.txt) and a short seed manifest. Proposed schedule: I will seed the project and admin key tomorrow (2026-11-19) morning PST and send the seeded-keys-manifest.csv privately. Marcus / Soojin — any blockers from your side?

From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@brightlyhealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dave Hernandez <dave.hernandez@brightlyhealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-19T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Brightly - implementation kickoff & access / API key plan

Thanks for the clear breakdown. Morning PST on 11/30 works for us. A couple notes from Brightly infra: 
- We'll bring Okta and want to tie admin console SSO to our Okta Org. Can Connor or Soojin share the SAML metadata endpoint ahead of the call?
- For keys, we'd prefer customer-managed KMS; Dave can share the ARN.
- For early automation we will probably want a service-account JSON with short-lived credentials (rotation supported by our infra).

If you can seed the admin key on 11/19 as proposed, we can validate basic connectivity ahead of the kickoff.

Sara
Sara Patel
Director, Platform Engineering | Brightly Health
sara.patel@brightlyhealth.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@brightlyhealth.com>, Dave Hernandez <dave.hernandez@brightlyhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Brightly - implementation kickoff & access / API key plan

On Wed, Nov 18, 2026 at 4:12 PM Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Marcus — can you confirm the default RBAC roles and whether we need the "service-account" pattern for telemetry ingestion, or if a scoped API key is sufficient?

Quick tech note from my side: 
- Default roles: Project Admin, Project Engineer (limited write), Telemetry Writer (ingest-only), and Readonly Auditor.
- For automated telemetry ingestion at scale we strongly recommend a short-lived service-account with a rotating secret (we provide rotation hooks via the Key Manager integration). Scoped write-only API keys are OK for POC but make rotation and audit-trail linking harder.
- If Brightly will use customer-managed KMS, we'll need the KMS ARN plus an IAM role we can assume to encrypt/decrypt the seed blob. Otherwise, Redwood-managed envelope encryption is fine for the pilot.

I'll be available during the seeding window to validate permissions. I'll also add a short checklist for recommended role mappings (will drop into the drive link).

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@brightlyhealth.com>, Dave Hernandez <dave.hernandez@brightlyhealth.com>

Subject: Re: Brightly - implementation kickoff & access / API key plan

All — quick update ahead of the kickoff: 
- I've created the 'brightly-prod' project in us-west and seeded the admin key (admin:project) and telemetry key (telemetry:ingest). Attached is the seeded-keys-manifest.csv with the masked key IDs (we'll share the full secret via the secure docs channel in a separate message).
- For SSO/SAML: Soojin will send the SAML metadata endpoint and a short Okta guide by EOD.
- Marcus validated the RBAC mapping; he dropped a checklist in the Drive (link above).

Action items: 
- Brightly: share KMS ARN and the Okta metadata before 11/30 kick-off.
- Redwood: Connor to publish the admin invite link and Soojin to share SAML metadata (both by 2026-11-24 EOD).

Calendar: https://calendar.redwood.ai/event/0a1b2c3d-brightly-kickoff

Thanks — Connor
